propositions: Rebar must support provider-native authentication for Bedrock, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gerrit, GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, and Jira across local, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, and AWS-hosted environments without implementing a universal secret broker or weakening SDK-owned credential refresh and rotation.

Static unavoidable credentials must use provider-specific non-serializable containers with SecretStr/SecretBytes masking, excluded from operation snapshots and serialization, with values unwrapped only at the sending adapter boundary.

Deployment resolves external secret stores (SSM, files, or environment) before process startup; Rebar consumes provider-native capabilities and adapter-scoped static material; static credential rotation occurs via restart or redeploy without application-owned polling, hot-reload caching, or secret-file watching.

Subprocess children inherit ambient environment for trusted same-capability cases; Rebar materializes static credentials only for owning children, removes exact declared secret names from unrelated siblings, never mutates global os.environ, and relies on deployment step/container/service scoping as the primary security boundary.

Application operation snapshots remain non-secret; Rebar-owned factories construct and own official SDK clients while accepting provider-native credential, identity, or session capabilities; no arbitrary fully constructed clients that bypass Rebar retry, timeout, cache, or output policy are accepted in the initial public seam.

Op-certificate signing accepts exactly one of REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH (file, preferred) or REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY (multiline environment); no runtime AWS/SSM coupling, per-job boto3 retrieval, SsmKeyFetcher, or application-owned credential provisioning exists in the approved design.
